Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.kwebdemo1.nodes

Class BasicNode

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.kwebdemo1.nodes.BasicNode
Direct Known Subclasses:
JourneyNode
public class BasicNode extends Object
Base class for nodes. Nodes identify a specific person, thing or event in history in the Knowledge Web graph.
Since:
JDK 1.5.0, Java3D 1.4.0, lg3d-{core,demo,incubator} 0.7.0

    • global

      protected NodeData global
      Reference to a the NodeData singleton which contains some common utils. I should have probably put that in a utils class. Haven't decided what I want to do quite yet.

    • id

      protected int id

    • name

      protected String name
      URL name (XML bio id) for this node.

    • cent

      protected int cent
      Century this node belongs to. This is normally specified by a derived class as a CENTURY constant.

    • rho

      public double rho
      In spherical coordinates, the Euclidean distance between the center of the coordinate system and the point. Would be safer to call this the radial distance or coordinate. Some texts call it 'r' for radius.

    • theta

      public double theta
      theta is the counter-clockwise angle (looking from above) along the horizontal plane starting from the axis pointing toward the viewer (z). Some math texts define phi for this so it can get confusing. A value of pi/2 (90 degrees) is aligned with the axis going right (x). Would be safer to call this the azimuthal angle or coordinate. Same as longitude.

    • phi

      public double phi
      phi is the angle starting at the polar vector (y). A value of pi/2 (90 degrees) means the point is located on the equator. Beware, some texts reverse theta and phi. Would be safer to call this the "polar" angle or coordinate (also known as colatitude). Same as latitude if you subtract a 90 degree offset.

    • displayedEdges

      public ArrayList<DisplayedEdge> displayedEdges
      The list of displayed edges connected to this node. The node may be connected to other edges which are not displayed. This is because a lot of edges are directional in both directions, e.g. "A taught B" and "B was student of A". However, to reduce display overhead, only one of these edges is actually displayed.

      This is public but shouldn't be. I was running out of time and needed to get things done quickly rather than correctly. Sigh...

  • Constructor Details

    • BasicNode

      public BasicNode(NodeData global, int id, String name, int cent, double theta, double phi, String oneLiner)
      Creates a KWeb node with all the info it needs to be rendered on a graph.
      Parameters:
      global - reference to class holding shared data.
      id - ID number needed by the GraphAEL layout system. This assigned by an external script.
      name - URL-encoded ID used in the KWeb XML bios.
      cent - Which onionskin this node is assigned to by century. Gateway nodes are assigned to century 0.
      theta - angle around vertical-axis (y) in radians of node position
      phi - angle from vertical-axis (y) in radians of node position
      oneLiner - brief description of node contents

    • getCartesianPosition

      public org.jogamp.vecmath.Point3d getCartesianPosition()
      Get the x,y,z position in Java 3D coordinates of this node. There is no standard consenses of which Cartesian coordinate translates to which spherical coordinate. In text books, the z-axis is shown as the vertical axis and the x and y axies make up the horizontal plane. However, most computer display systems show the Y-axis as vertical (as in 2-D systems) and the Z-axis represents depth, though some (like Pixel-3D) specify positive z as farther away, while others (like Java3D) specify positive z as toward the viewer. These equations have been adjusted to use the Java3D coordinate system. Conversions:
      Coordinate orientation Text book and Perl coordinate Java3D and LookingGlass coordinate
      Towards right y x
      Upward z y
      Towards viewer x z
      Returns:
      the point position of this node
